title: A customized framework for regional classification of conifers using automated feature extraction
author: Roth, Coates, et al.

steps.title: Create training polygons
steps.instruction: Review each NAIP tile for conifers, then digitize a representative sample of conifer image objects to build a training polygon set (minimum five polygons per tile; each polygon must contain at least three cells and represent a canopy height of ≥ 3 m). Distinguish conifers by the hue of red in traditional false‑color settings and verify identifications with Google Earth™ version 7.1.2.2041 (2013).

steps.title: Set wizard parameters and classify
steps.instruction: In Feature Analyst™ Supervised Learning Wizard, load the training polygons and specify: “Natural Feature” selector with “Bullseye 3” over a 25‑m² moving window; enable “Natural Shape” to avoid hard‑line objects; set pattern width to 5 m (matching the Bullseye window). Run the supervised learning algorithm on the four‑band NAIP image to generate conifer features, aggregating any detected features larger than 3 m².

steps.title: Assess initial classification
steps.instruction: Compare the output conifer features to the NAIP reference imagery. If the result is under‑classified, digitize additional training polygons and rerun the supervised classification. For extremely dense stands, execute multiple learning algorithms on the same tile and merge their outputs. If the result is over‑classified, digitize samples of incorrect, correct, and missed features for further refinement.

steps.title: Hierarchical learning and cleanup
steps.instruction: Perform hierarchical supervised classification using three sub‑processes: (1) digitize incorrect features for removal with the “Begin Removing Clutter Tool” (include shadows, riparian vegetation, and other non‑conifer features); (2) identify correct output features to retrain the OBIA algorithm; (3) digitize missed features and add them with the “Begin Adding Missed Features Tool.” After hierarchical learning, dissolve overlapping polygons, repair geometry, and delete features smaller than 3 m². Remove large misclassifications (e.g., algae, irrigated fields, wet meadows, riparian areas, other non‑conifer vegetation) using custom polygon masks, then convert the cleaned shapefiles to 2‑bit binary VHSR rasters with 1‑m² cells.

substeps.instruction: Digitize incorrect features and remove with “Begin Removing Clutter Tool”.
Identify correct features and retrain the OBIA algorithm.
Digitize missed features and add with “Begin Adding Missed Features Tool”.
Dissolve overlapping features and repair polygon geometry.
Mask large misclassifications using custom polygons.
Convert cleaned shapefiles to 2‑bit binary VHSR rasters (1‑m² cells).

steps.title: Final review and mosaic
steps.instruction: Review each tile for omission and commission errors and inspect neighboring tiles for seamlines; re‑analyze any tile with pervasive seamlines. Once raster outputs are deemed clean, mosaic the tiles for each zone or PMU in ERDAS Imagine (2013, Leica Geosystems, Atlanta, GA) using the “Automatic Most Nadir Seam” setting to minimize seamlines by overlapping areas equidistant from image centers.
